Changelog

All packages version together. Entries are generated from changesets on release; this file also records protocol-level changes by hand.

0.1.0 (unreleased)

Initial release of the Body Spray SDK and the axe/0.1 protocol.

  • spec/: AXE-PROTOCOL.md, KINDS.md, EVENTS.md, VOCABULARY.md, generated JSON Schemas.
  • @axe/core: createAXE, action, result envelope, escalation ladder with signed tokens, idempotency, auth modes with login handoff, multi-tenant manifests and platform index, display and affordance validation, well-known kinds, honesty lints, events and sinks.
  • @axe/client: discovery, invoke/continue/resume/poll, run() with fulfillers, present/toMarkdown/toHTML.
  • @axe/mcp: derived MCP server over stdio and Streamable HTTP.
  • @axe/express, @axe/next, @axe/fetch: adapters.
  • @axe/testing: conformance suite, AXE audit, vocabulary drift check, test helpers.
  • axe CLI: init, validate, inspect, preview, conformance, audit, mcp.

Request policy (review item 6)

  • Protocol §6.4, [P-TRANS-1] to [P-TRANS-4]: a POST to a state-changing endpoint (an action that is not readOnly, /axe/continue, /axe/resume) must be application/json or application/*+json, else unsupported; a POST carrying ambient credentials from an origin that is neither the site's (from baseUrl, never Host or forwarded headers) nor trusted is forbidden, the same response for every path; requests with neither Origin nor Sec-Fetch-Site pass the origin rule.
  • @axe/core: createAXE({ requestPolicy: { requireJsonContentType, trustedOrigins, originCheck } }), applied at the entry of handle() before any body, identity, or token is read. Defaults: JSON required on writes; origin checked on any POST with a Cookie header; origins with credentialed cors trusted. Refusals carry details.reason json_required or cross_origin_refused. Pure functions exported (evaluateRequestPolicy, resolveRequestPolicy, isJsonContentType, isAcceptedOrigin). Migration: a caller that posts JSON to a mutating action without Content-Type: application/json now gets unsupported; @axe/client, @axe/mcp, and the conformance suite already send the header.
  • @axe/express and @axe/next (Pages): the adapters keep the Content-Type the client sent instead of relabeling a parsed body as JSON, and the Express adapter reads the raw stream while it is unread (Express 4 leaves req.body = {} on a body its json parser skipped).
  • @axe/testing: conformance check runtime.json-content-type.

Surface

  • spec/SURFACE.md: the Surface contract (v0.2), ported from the sumapps trials and rewritten on top of the AXE envelope: live controls with state.reason, effect as AXE risk metadata, one revision per application, refusals as conflict / not_found / invalid_input / unavailable, and requires (AXE kinds) plus handoff on unavailable controls.
  • @axe/surface: createSurface (registry, observe, act, revision, ledger, expose), @axe/surface/react (useSurface), and @axe/surface/axe (surfaceActions: any surface becomes an AXE manifest with <ns>.observe, <ns>.ledger, and one action per entry, refusals mapped onto the ladder, continue running the application's fulfill).
  • Vocabulary: a "Surface" section in spec/VOCABULARY.md (entry kinds, ops, field names, API names) so the drift test covers the new package.
  • Two defects from the first staging trial pinned as contract rules with tests: act refuses any target that is not a non-empty id or a non-negative integer index as invalid_input before any lookup, an index never resolves to a row without one, and the revision guard runs before resolution ([S-ACT-6..8]); applications must re-register on transient states ([S-REV-5]), with freeze(reason) / thaw as the first-class helper: every entry unavailable with the reason, observe().frozen, acts unavailable, revision moved on both ends, nested freezes counted ([S-FRZ-1..4]).
  • DOM mirror: surfaceAttributes, surfaceSelector, and describeEntry in @axe/surface, and useSurfaceProps in @axe/surface/react, so the accessible name a browser agent or screen reader reads is the entry name by construction. Spec §7 is now a rule set: [S-DOM-1] (name wording and the attribute set), [S-DOM-3] (the selector contract), [S-DOM-4] (the one-line description); a domAttribute vocabulary category names the attributes.
  • Ledger (spec/SURFACE.md [S-LED-1..7]): every act, run or refused, appends { seq, at, op, target, actor, revBefore, revAfter, status, text?, changed }; ledger({ since, actor, limit }) reads it oldest first under bounded retention (ledger.max, default 1000); observe() carries ledgerSeq and every act result its seq; expose publishes ledger. The bridge adds <ns>.ledger (read-only, with display) and emits one action event (surface.act) per act on the server's onActionEvent sinks ([S-AXE-4]). In @axe/core: action events (spec/EVENTS.md [E-5..7], schemas/action-event.schema.json), emit on the handler context, onActionEvent on createAXE, and consoleSink/jsonlFileSink accept them.

Live state

  • Protocol §21 (additive, still axe/0.1): a site MAY publish a revision. Every result envelope gains optional top-level rev; requests to /axe/actions/{name}, /axe/continue, and /axe/resume gain optional expectedRev; a stale expectedRev is conflict with details: { expectedRev, currentRev } and nothing applied, checked after the idempotency replay and before the handler or a login handoff. Actions gain optional availability ({ available, reason?, requires?, handoff? }), the manifest gains live: { rev?, url? }, and GET /axe/state serves { rev?, actions } per caller with Cache-Control: no-store. unavailable errors MAY carry details: { reason, requires?, handoff? }. Rules P-LIVE-1 to P-LIVE-10; spec/schemas/state.schema.json.
  • @axe/core: createAXE({ revision }), action({ availability }), handler context availability and expectedRev, unavailable() helper, describeLive(), lint rule unavailable-without-reason.
  • @axe/client: expectedRev on invoke, continue, resume, and run (tracked through the ladder), state(), live(), stateToMarkdown; present carries rev into toMarkdown and toHTML.
  • @axe/mcp: axe_state tool when the manifest carries live, expectedRev argument on action tools, availability in tool descriptions, stale conflict and unavailable explained.
  • @axe/testing: six live.* conformance checks (skipped without live), audit check actionable.live-state.
  • @axe/surface: a stale act's details are { expectedRev, currentRev } (was { rev, expectedRev }); surfaceActions reads the envelope's expectedRev; pass revision: surface.currentRev to createAXE.

Surface: one action per control (contract v0.3)

  • spec/SURFACE.md §6 rewritten: every entry is its own AXE action ([S-AXE-1], [S-AXE-6]), named <ns>.<slug> by a deterministic, collision-safe, reversible rule ([S-AXE-7]), with the entry's live state as its availability ([S-AXE-8]) and the set following the registry ([S-AXE-9]). [S-OBS-3] adds entries(), registryVersion(), and availability(id) to the surface.
  • Removed before any release: the generic <ns>.act action of contract v0.2, its target/op input, and the deprecated input.expectedRev. The revision travels only as the request envelope's expectedRev; observe's per-row affordances name the row's own action and carry expectedRev for the envelope.
  • @axe/surface/axe: surfaceActions returns an ActionProvider (axe.addProvider(surfaceActions(surface))) with actionNameFor, entryIdFor, and onChange; entrySlug exported; options fields (risk and reversibility declared for field entries) and onError (an entry whose text fails the honesty lint is reported and left out). observe and ledger carry examples, so the conformance suite's live.* checks run against a surface.
  • @axe/core: ActionProvider, axe.addProvider(provider), and axe.onActionsChanged(listener); providers are consulted after registered actions wherever actions are enumerated or looked up, with name uniqueness and auth modes still checked. A retried idempotencyKey for an action that has since left the set is answered from the idempotency store before not_found ([P-IDEM-2]). Dynamic affordances may carry expectedRev ([P-AFF-4]; DynamicAffordance, ResolvedAffordance, schemas/manifest.schema.json).
  • @axe/mcp: for an in-process AXE source the tool list is derived on every tools/list, tool calls resolve against the current manifest (with an idempotency key supplied for mutating actions the client's snapshot did not know), and the server declares the list-changed capability and sends notifications/tools/list_changed when onActionsChanged fires.

Surface: integration fixes (contract v0.4)

What the first integration into a legacy-DOM application asked for, made general.

  • Browser bundling: jsonlFileSink moves to @axe/core/node, the one entry of @axe/core that needs Node; it is no longer exported from @axe/core or @axe/core/events. A browser bundle importing @axe/surface no longer meets fs/promises. New zod-free subpath @axe/core/json-schema (validateJsonSchema, schemasStructurallyEqual, deepEqual). A bundle test in packages/surface/test builds @axe/surface plus @axe/surface/react for the browser with esbuild and fails on a Node built-in, on Zod, or above 50 kB minified (about 21 kB today, from a build that failed and, with the built-in aliased away, 515 kB).
  • Zod-free surface ([S-ENT-3]): @axe/surface and @axe/surface/react import nothing that carries Zod. edit.schema is a JSON Schema or a Zod schema; a Zod schema is detected structurally (safeParse), validated by calling it, and published in observe() through createSurface({ toJsonSchema }) (pass toJsonSchema from @axe/core), which the requires schemas from accept() need too. Registering a Zod schema without the converter throws with that instruction. @axe/surface/axe still carries Zod through @axe/core.
  • Revision modes ([S-REV-1], [S-FRZ-2], [S-FRZ-3]): surface (the application calls bump) or app (it adopts a server revision with setRev), inferred from the last call or pinned with createSurface({ revision }); revisionMode() reports it. In app mode freeze and thaw leave the revision alone and still report the freeze and notify onChange, so an act planned before a freeze is unavailable while frozen and accepted after the thaw exactly when the application's revision did not move.
  • Handler reports ([S-ACT-1], [S-LED-5]): a handler, edit.set, or more may return { changed?, rev? }; act folds changed into the output and the ledger and adopts rev as setRev would before building the result. HandlerReport type.
  • Live DOM mirror ([S-DOM-1]): surface.attributesFor(id) returns { set, remove } from the live availability, so a freeze shows with its reason and a stale reason is removed; SURFACE_ATTRIBUTES lists every attribute the mirror may set. surfaceAttributes(entry) stays for a one-time render. useSurfaceProps follows the live availability and re-renders when it changes.
  • Bridge ([S-AXE-2], [S-AXE-6], [S-LED-1]): a collection without more has no action (it stays a row of observe); entry input schemas describe the shape only (text a string, confirm an optional boolean), leaving maxLength, the field's schema, and a required confirm to the surface so every such refusal is ledgered and emitted; needs_human only for a handoff with a url.
  • Handoff without a url ([S-AV-3]; protocol [P-LIVE-5], [P-LIVE-9]): HandoffSpec.url is optional on an unavailable action's handoff, for a step taken inside the application with no page of its own. It is reported in availability and in error.details.handoff and never becomes needs_human, whose Handoff stays complete ([P-HAND-1]). spec/schemas/state.schema.json and manifest.schema.json follow.
  • createAXE defaults auth to { modes: ["none"] }; an explicit empty modes is refused with a message that says to omit auth for a public site.
  • Consuming from a checkout: scripts/pack-for-consumer.sh <out-dir> builds and packs core, surface, client, and testing and writes a SOURCE file; docs/deploying.md ("Consume from a checkout") covers file: dependencies, the overrides for packed siblings, and copying tarballs into place before installing from a lockfile.
  • Vocabulary: attributesFor, revisionMode, SURFACE_ATTRIBUTES; jsonlFileSink now under @axe/core/node.

Surface: write preconditions (contract v0.5)

  • Ordering ([S-ACT-9]): acts on one surface run one at a time, in call order. Every pre-handler check runs when act is called, so a refusal never waits; an act that waits behind another is checked again when it reaches execution (revision, target, freeze, availability), and is conflict or unavailable with no handler run when a predecessor's commit, a person's bump or setRev, or a freeze intervened. Before, two asynchronous acts presenting the same expectedRev both ran and both returned ok. observe, availability, and ledger do not wait.
  • A commit that leaves an app-owned revision in place ([S-ACT-10]) closes the claims taken before it at that revision, unless it provably changed nothing (changed: []); an act claimed after it is accepted.
  • The handler's own precondition ([S-ACT-11]): handlers, field setters, and more receive an ActContext ({ id, op, expectedRev, actor }) as their last argument for a conditional write, and refuse by throwing SurfaceConflict (new export) or returning { conflict: { currentRev? } } in the HandlerReport; act returns conflict with details.currentRev, ledgers a refusal, and adopts nothing.
  • A stale handler report ([S-REV-6]): a reported rev lower than the surface's revision when the handler settles is not adopted; the ledger entry carries it as ignoredRev (also in <ns>.ledger output).
  • Bridge ([S-AXE-4]): the entry action passes the envelope's expectedRev to the queued act, so the server's check is the first gate and the surface's the second; a test drives two concurrent invocations through axe.handle.
  • Vocabulary: SurfaceConflict, ActContext, ignoredRev, the handler report's conflict.

Surface: authorization and privacy (contract v0.5)

  • spec/SURFACE.md §6.1 ([S-AUTH-1] to [S-AUTH-6], [S-PRV-1] to [S-PRV-3]); [S-LED-1] and [S-DOM-2] updated. From the 2026-09-24 review, item 5.
  • @axe/surface/axe: every generated action declares auth, default user; a server whose auth.modes lacks user (including createAXE's public default) refuses the bridge on its first request. Options auth, read (observe and ledger), authFor(entry), template, redactEvent. surfaceActions accepts a resolver (context) => Surface | null in place of a surface, with a template for the action set; scopedSurfaces({ create, key, max, idleMs, now, onEvict }) builds one keyed by tenant and principal. Availability for an unidentified caller never reads a protected surface. Types SurfaceContext, SurfaceResolver, ScopedSurfaces, ScopedSurfacesOptions.
  • @axe/surface: field entries take sensitive: true (no value in observe(), describeEntry says value hidden, no ledger text); createSurface({ ledger: { text: "keep" | "hash" | "omit", redact } }); ledger entries may carry textHash. Types LedgerOptions, LedgerTextPolicy.
  • Migration: a bridge that should stay public passes auth: "none"; otherwise add user (or site) to the server's auth.modes. Docs examples now pass auth explicitly.
  • Vocabulary: scopedSurfaces, authFor, redactEvent, idleMs, onEvict, keyFor, textHash; sensitive also names the Surface field flag.

Surface: mounted React behavior (contract v0.6)

  • @axe/surface/react, useSurface and useSurfaceProps (review item 11): the registration belongs to the entry's id and the target surface. A change of either unregisters the previous pair and registers the new one; before, an id change left the old id registered (and unmount then removed the old id, leaving the new one), and a target change registered nothing in the new surface. An act now runs the latest render's handler, edit.set, more, and requires.fulfill through a stable wrapper, whatever deps list; before, it ran the closure from the render that last changed deps. Registration runs in a layout effect (a passive effect on the server). useSurfaceProps subscribes once rather than on every render.
  • @axe/surface: surface.subscribe(listener) ([S-OBS-4], additive): called after every register, an unregister or reconcile that removed a row, bump, setRev, a seedRev that adopted a revision, freeze, thaw, and reset. useSurfaceProps reads through it, so a registration made outside the component reaches the control. onChange is unchanged and still does not fire on registration, so the bridge's change notification (and MCP tools/list_changed) is not sent once per row.
  • spec/SURFACE.md v0.6: [S-OBS-4]; [S-ENT-5] and [S-DOM-1] state the React hooks' ownership, latest-handler, and Strict Mode rules.
  • Tests: packages/surface/test/react-mounted.test.ts mounts the hooks with react-dom/client under jsdom (jsdom is a devDependency of @axe/surface only; the bundle test checks it never enters the browser bundle). The browser bundle of @axe/surface and /react went from 25,290 to 26,308 bytes minified.
  • Migration: none required. Code that listed handler inputs in deps only to keep the closure fresh can drop them. Code that relied on an id change keeping the old row (no known consumer) must register the old id itself. A non-React mirror that re-applies attributesFor on onChange should use subscribe under an application-owned revision.
  • Vocabulary: subscribe.
  • Bridge change notifications (follow-up): the provider's onChange now listens on subscribe, so a row that registers or leaves under an app-owned revision announces a changed action set (MCP tools/list_changed) with no bump; notifications are coalesced to one per microtask and still fire only when registryVersion moved.
  • Bridge change notifications, second follow-up (review item 16): onChange compares the published definitions and notifies only when they differ, so a re-render that re-registers rows unchanged sends nothing (46 notifications over 50 scripted UI changes fell to about 20, none empty).

Generate

  • @axe/generate: derive AXE actions from definitions an application already has, so the manifest follows the definition instead of being written beside it. fromOpenAPI maps every OpenAPI 3.x operation to an action (name from the operationId or the method and path, flags and default risk by method, auth from the security requirements, input from parameters plus the JSON request body, output from the 2xx response, an HTTP handler that maps upstream statuses to AXE error codes) with an in-house JSON Schema → Zod converter for the common subset. fromFunctions takes a table of zod-typed functions; fromTRPCRouter reads a tRPC router structurally, without depending on tRPC. generate merges sources, applies per-action overrides and a policy (exclude, include, defaultRisk, maxRisk, requireInputDescriptions), runs the honesty lints, and returns actions, warnings, and provenance; registerGenerated registers the result.
  • Honesty: the generator never invents a description, a risk for a mutation, a display shape, or a human URL. An operation missing one is left out with a warning naming the operation and the field, until an override supplies it.
  • axe generate <openapi.json> [--base-url] [--out axe.json] [--code axe.ts]: prints what was generated and why anything was left out, writes a static manifest for review, and emits a starter module with one TODO per gap. JSON input only.
  • Docs: docs/generating.md. Vocabulary: axe generate and the @axe/generate API names.

Website

  • site/: a static marketing and documentation site built from docs/, spec/, and the root Markdown files. Runs from file:// with no network; site/dist/ is committed and reproducible. Landing page with the escalation-ladder demo (real envelopes), the search → present → select demo (real toHTML() output), an embedded axe audit report, and a docs hub generated from docs/README.md. Tests: reproducible build, offline load in Chromium/Firefox/WebKit, link check, demo behavior, responsive screenshots, Lighthouse ≥ 95.

llms.txt

  • llms.txt at the repository root: an integration guide for agents, in the llms.txt convention (an H1, a summary, H2 sections of links with one-line descriptions). Sections: what this is and the three Surface rules, decide your shape, rules that are scars, packaging, ship behind a flag, tests to write, reading order, API at a glance, what does not exist yet. The site build writes site/dist/llms.txt (links rewritten to the published pages) and site/dist/llms-full.txt (the index followed by every doc and spec page in navigation order); a site test checks that every link resolves and every page is carried.

Client trust boundary (review 2026-09-24, item 3)

  • Protocol §17.1, [P-AGENT-4] to [P-AGENT-9]: agent-side rules for where requests and credentials may go. Additive; no wire change.
  • @axe/client: credentials (auth and headers) go only to the discovery origin (or, for a manifest passed to new AXEClient, its baseUrl origin) plus trust.origins. A baseUrl, live.url, pollUrl, AXE-Manifest header, or axe-manifest link on another origin is refused, or contacted without credentials when trust.allowCrossOrigin is set (loopback and private-range names stay refused). Redirects are followed by hand and re-checked per hop; credentials never cross an origin on a redirect; https-to-http is refused. Plain http only for authorized loopback origins by default (trust.allowHttp). trust.destinationPolicy gates every outbound URL. Refusals throw AXETrustError before anything is sent; checkDestination(url) answers without sending. AXEClient.discover throws when the manifest's baseUrl is not authorized. Behavior change: a client that relied on a cross-origin baseUrl, live.url, or pollUrl must list the origin in trust.origins; in browsers, a redirect is refused because its target cannot be checked.
  • @axe/mcp: axe_poll polls only a pollUrl the server returned in a pending result; any other URL is refused without a request. Tool schema unchanged.

Review 2026-09-24: token binding, site principals, operations

  • Tokens ([P-TOK-6], [P-TOK-7]): every continue, resume, and poll is checked against the serving tenant and the acting principal before any hook runs or any stored result is returned; every refusal is the unknown-token not_found. A continuation minted on one tenant no longer runs on another. A token minted anonymously is refused with a user's credentials. completeHandoff takes tenant and refuses another tenant's handoff, a used one, a different user on a user-bound handoff, and a second user on a login handoff.
  • Site keys: one principal for invoke, continue, resume, and poll, so a workflow started with a site key continues with it (it was not_found). A verdict without an id is scoped by an HMAC of the key. Keys are verified again on every follow-up. siteKey (SiteKeyContext: id, actions, derived) reaches onContinue, onResume, onPoll, availability hooks, and the revision provider (RevisionContext.identity, RevisionContext.siteKey).
  • Poll ([P-POLL-1], [P-POLL-2]): authorized before a terminal result is returned (it was readable anonymously); one onPoll at a time per token.
  • Operations (§12.2, [P-OP-1] to [P-OP-4]): IdempotencyStore is now get, claim, complete, release (breaking; no shim; createAXE refuses a get/set store). Concurrent calls with one key, and concurrent uses of one token, run once; the others get a retryable conflict with details.operationStatus: "in_progress" and Retry-After. A repeated successful continue or resume returns its original envelope instead of conflict ([P-REQ-9], [P-HAND-6]). operationLeaseSeconds config; operationId on handler contexts. SqliteIdempotencyStore in @axe/core/node. TokenRecord.onBehalfOf is now principal; consumedAt and terminal are removed.
  • Conformance: ladder.continue-replay and ladder.resume-replay expect the original envelope; new ladder.token-principal.

MCP over HTTP and remote freshness (review 2026-09-24, items 9 and 10)

  • Protocol §22, [P-MCP-1] to [P-MCP-5]: rules for a bridge to MCP (HTTP lifecycle, per-request identity and session binding, poll scope, remote freshness, retry keys). [P-DISC-13]: the manifest carries an ETag, If-None-Match gets 304, and an agent revalidates a cached manifest past its max-age. Additive; no wire change for existing requests.
  • @axe/mcp: serveHttp served one client in total (a stateless transport was reused and the second HTTP request failed; a stateful one could not initialize a second client). It now builds a server and transport per request (stateless, the default) or per session (sessions), with DELETE, idle expiry (idleTimeoutMs, default 30 minutes) answered 404, maxSessions, close(), and sessionCount. auth makes the endpoint an OAuth resource server (verifier, requiredScopes, resource, resourceMetadataUrl); clientFor(authInfo) gives each tool call its caller's own AXE identity; sessions are bound to the principal that opened them; protectedResourceMetadata serves the RFC 9728 document; allowedOrigins guards against DNS rebinding. axe_poll URLs are scoped per session or per principal. URL and manifest sources refresh the manifest within its bound, on an unknown tool name, and after not_found, and send notifications/tools/list_changed; refresh() on the derived server. Mutating tools take an optional idempotencyKey; axe_continue and axe_resume take expectedRev. axe_poll fetches at once instead of waiting a second first.
  • @axe/client: refresh(), ensureFresh(), isManifestStale(), onManifestChange(), ManifestChange, and the manifestMaxAgeMs option; run() refetches once for an unknown action.
  • @axe/core: ETag on the manifest and 304 for a matching If-None-Match.
  • Migration: serveHttp now throws when createMcpServer was given client.auth or client.headers and no clientFor (every HTTP caller would act as that user); pass allowSharedCredentials: true for a single-user endpoint. serveHttp takes the object createMcpServer returned, as before; sessionIdGenerator still works and is deprecated in favor of sessions.

Review 2026-09-24, item 12: limits, schema boundaries, retention

  • Protocol §6.5, [P-LIM-1] to [P-LIM-4]: request bodies are bounded before they are read in full, refused with invalid_input, details.reason: "payload_too_large", details.maxBodyBytes, and HTTP 413 ([P-INV-6] amended for the status); deep nesting gets an envelope, never a server error; agents bound time, response size, and polling (a floor of one second between polls); stores remove expired records whether or not they are read again and never evict a running claim.
  • Protocol §5.4, [P-SCHEMA-1] to [P-SCHEMA-6]: the supported JSON Schema subset; validators check own members only and refuse values under constructs they cannot apply; exact decimal multipleOf; ECMAScript patterns without catastrophic backtracking; x-axe-refined on schema nodes the server checks more strictly than JSON Schema can say; the idempotency fingerprint is input as sent.
  • @axe/core: maxBodyBytes (default 1 MiB), enforced from Content-Length and while reading the stream; bodies nested deeper than 64 levels are invalid_input (they overflowed the stack while hashing). MemoryTokenStore and MemoryIdempotencyStore take now, maxEntries (default 10000), and sweepIntervalMs (default 60000), sweep expired entries on writes, evict oldest first without evicting a running claim, and gain sweep() and close(). SqliteIdempotencyStore.prune(before?), with an index on expires.
  • @axe/core JSON Schema validator: __proto__, constructor, and other inherited names no longer slip past additionalProperties: false or satisfy required; circular refs, non-local refs, plain-name fragments, patterns that do not compile, formats it cannot check, and keywords outside the subset are issues instead of a stack overflow, a thrown SyntaxError, or silent acceptance; patternProperties, propertyNames, min/maxProperties, dependentRequired, dependentSchemas, uniqueItems, contains, min/maxContains, and if/then/else are implemented; ipv4 and jwt formats. schemaProblems, isBacktrackingPattern, compilePattern, and SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_KEYWORDS exported. Lint rules unsupported-schema, backtracking-pattern, refined-schema.
  • @axe/core fingerprints: the idempotency fingerprint and token input binding hash input as sent, not the parsed value. Fixes a transform to a Date (or anything JSON cannot carry) fingerprinting every input the same, so a reused key with different input replayed the first result instead of conflict; a login handoff now stores the raw input, so a transform no longer runs twice (the resume failed with invalid_input). Migration: a retry across the upgrade whose raw input differs from its parsed input (a stripped unknown member, a default) gets conflict once; an agent that resends the same body is unaffected.
  • @axe/express, @axe/next (Pages): an unread body stream is read only up to maxBodyBytes + 1 bytes (nothing when Content-Length is larger) and the connection is closed after the 413; they buffered the whole body before. toWebRequest takes { maxBodyBytes }.
  • @axe/client: timeoutMs (default 30 s) and maxResponseBytes (default 4 MiB) on the client and discover; a caller signal on every public method, including discover and AXEClient.discover (third argument); maxPollAttempts (default 60), and maxWaitMs shared by every poll of one run(); retryAfter clamped to at least one second. Manifests, results, and live-state documents are checked for the members the client uses, and a malformed one is an AXEClientError naming the member (a needs_input without accepts used to crash run() with a TypeError). Bundle budget 18 kB (was 15 kB).
  • @axe/generate: a format no longer drops minLength, maxLength, and pattern; an additionalProperties schema beside properties is a catchall, not "anything"; a pattern that does not compile, an unchecked format, and keywords outside the subset are unsupported-schema warnings.
  • @axe/testing: conformance checks runtime.body-limit and runtime.nesting-limit.
  • Docs: new page Schemas: the supported subset; docs/deploying.md "Limits and retention"; docs/for-agent-builders.md "Timeouts, cancellation, and budgets"; DoS and backtracking rows in docs/security.md.

Review 2026-09-24, item 14: existing agent interfaces through adapters

  • @axe/surface/webmcp (new subpath, experimental): exposeWebMcp(surface, options) registers an observe tool and one tool per actionable control with document.modelContext.registerTool (WebMCP Community Group draft of 2026-09-17), re-registers on subscribe when a tool's text, schema, or hints change, never offers a sensitive field, and runs each call through surface.act with the call's expectedRev or the current revision. Without WebMCP it registers nothing and returns supported: false with the reason. Not imported by @axe/surface or /react; about 5.6 kB minified on top of the main entry. Spec: spec/SURFACE.md v0.7, §8, [S-WEB-1] to [S-WEB-5].
  • @axe/mcp elicitation ([P-MCP-6], [P-MCP-7]): with a client that declared elicitation and a connection that can carry a server request (stdio, in-memory, HTTP sessions), a needs_input whose first suitable kind is not sensitive and fits MCP's flat form subset is asked for in a form and continued with /axe/continue; decline, cancel, or failure returns the text as before. Sensitive kinds (sensitive: true, every payment.* and identity.*, credentials) never go in a form: with URL mode and a page from the site (a fallback, or a needs_human other than login_required) the page is offered in URL mode. Options elicitation (false, or { timeoutMs }, default ten minutes). Exports isSensitiveAccept, toFormSchema.
  • @axe/mcp MCP Apps view ([P-MCP-8], experimental): for hosts that declared io.modelcontextprotocol/ui with text/html;profile=mcp-app, tools for display actions carry _meta.ui.resourceUri: "ui://axe/presentation", resources/list and resources/read serve a self-contained view, and ok results carry the toHTML rendering in _meta["axe/presentation"]. The server now declares the resources capability (empty list for other hosts). apps: false turns it off. formatResult takes an optional fourth argument.
  • Docs: new docs/webmcp.md; docs/mcp.md sections "Elicitation" and "MCP Apps view (experimental)", and "What does not map" rewritten to separate what MCP already provides (elicitation, Apps, OAuth resource-server authorization) from what AXE adds (typed kinds, the resumable ladder, revision guards, honesty and audit); the FAQ's comparison with MCP corrected the same way, and its OAuth answer now separates resource-server from authorization-server responsibilities.

Review 2026-09-24, items 13 and 15: execution modes, reference application, human oversight

  • Protocol §9.3, [P-APPR-1] to [P-APPR-9]: approval requests. A consequential call returns needs_human with reason: "approval_required"; the server records the input as sent and the relevant state beside the resume token's binding; only the site, from a person's session-authenticated and CSRF-protected request, records an approval, and only while the state still matches; the resume runs the recorded input once, only while the approval stands (approved, not cancelled, not invalidated, not expired, same principal and tenant, same state); a cancelled or invalidated request is conflict with details.handoffStatus cancelled or invalidated; a repeat returns the stored receipt; expiry defaults to one hour. §19 gains a consent bullet.
  • @axe/core: requestApproval (also on the handler's helpers), action({ approvalState }) (required with requestApproval; action() refuses it on a readOnly action or without onResume; the manifest gains humanHandoff: { reasons: ["approval_required"] }), ResumeContext.approval (ApprovalGrant: approved input, input as sent, bound state, approvedBy, times), AXE.getHandoff, AXE.approveHandoff, AXE.cancelHandoff (any unused handoff), types HandoffView, HandoffStatus, HandoffRefusal, HandoffDecision, ApprovalRequest, ApprovalRecord, ApprovalStateContext, constants APPROVAL_REQUIRED, APPROVAL_TTL_SECONDS. completeHandoff returns false for an approval request and for a cancelled handoff. The unknown resume token message now says nothing was applied and to start the action again.
  • spec/EVENTS.md "Approval events", [E-8]: the runtime emits approval.requested, approval.approved, approval.cancelled, approval.invalidated, and approval.executed on the onActionEvent sinks, with the request id and the actors and never the input, state, preview, or cancellation reason.
  • spec/SURFACE.md v0.7, §8 "Execution modes", [S-MODE-1] to [S-MODE-4]: a surface in a page belongs to that page instance and is reached only by code in the page; a server-side capability never depends on a browser closure; the SDK has no broker between the two; unmount unregisters and changes nothing on the server.
  • @axe/surface packaging: the /react entry imports the main entry (./index.js, or ./index.cjs for CommonJS) instead of inlining it, so the hooks' default target is the surface exported by @axe/surface; before, it was a second module-level registry that surface.expose(window) never showed.
  • examples/plan-review: a Next.js App Router reference application (private workspace package, outside pnpm -r build): per-tenant plans with a revision column and conditional writes, two people on two teams with session cookies under the request policy, server actions over AXE, browser-local controls on a page surface exposed at window.__surface, approve-and-lock through requestApproval and the app's own approval page, freeze and reopen, receipts, and one history. A Node suite (in pnpm -r test) and a Playwright suite (pnpm example:test:app). Root scripts example:dev, example:test, example:test:app.
  • Docs: new docs/human-oversight.md and docs/reference-app.md; docs/human-handoff.md (approvals and cancellation, the replay row corrected), docs/surface.md ("Where a surface runs"). The Plan Board demo points at the reference app and says its approval endpoint is not the SDK's approval primitive.

Review 2026-09-24, item 16: capability granularity (contract v0.8)

  • @axe/surface/axe: domainActions(surface, { namespace, domains }), a second granularity beside surfaceActions: a fixed set of parameterized actions (default set-field, run-control, load-more, or the application's own specs with covers, risk, idempotent, reversible, humanHandoff, idleReason), each taking { entryId, text?, confirm? } and running surface.act with the entry's own op, so the revision, ladder, ledger, and surface.act events are identical. An entry whose metadata exceeds its spec's, or whose text fails the honesty lint, is left uncovered and reported through onError. actionFor(entryId) and covered(name) report the map. spec/SURFACE.md [S-AXE-10] to [S-AXE-13].
  • <ns>.observe in both granularities takes object, kind, available, query, limit, and cursor, returns total and nextCursor, and declares pagination; page size 1000 (max 1000) per control, 50 (max 200) per domain action, set with the observe option (pageSize, maxPageSize). Rows keep registration order and their whole-observation index. surface.observe() is unchanged. [S-OBS-5]. Migration: none for callers of <ns>.observe without input on surfaces of up to 1000 rows; a larger surface now pages.
  • scripts/measure-granularity.mjs (pnpm measure:granularity): deterministic scripted measurements of both granularities at 5, 50, 300, and 1000 controls (manifest and tools/list size, tool churn and list_changed notifications, discovery cost, five scripted tasks verified against application state, and a two-actor conflict simulation); report in docs/review/2026-09-24/data/.
  • Docs: docs/surface.md "Choosing granularity"; DECISIONS.md entries on the two granularities, paged observe, and the per-entry revision proposal (not implemented).

Review 2026-09-24, item 18: audit claims and roadmap

  • @axe/testing audit: a skipped check earns nothing and reports earned: 0. A category in which every check skipped is not scored (new scored flag on each category, shown as "not scored") and the total is scaled to 100 over the scored categories; before, such a category earned its maximum, so a URL serving no manifest scored 80. presentable.pointers-resolve and trustworthy.tokens score only the halves that ran; describable.examples-validate skips when its conformance check did not run; checks with nothing to count (no actions, no input fields) skip. Fix-list points are in total-score points. Migration: a site where every Presentable check skipped, or one audited with the live round trip skipped and a failing static pointer check, may score differently; the getting-started tutorial scores 88 (was 89).
  • @axe/testing conformance: ladder.needs-human-avoidable skips when no needs_human was observed (it passed vacuously), and runtime.error-hygiene skips when no error body was seen. The table adds a line saying skipped checks were not verified and that conformance is not a security review.
  • Audit text and HTML reports end with "What this score is not": the counted and skipped checks, the conformance counts, and the limits (heuristic honesty checks, sampled parity, not a security review, not evidence of task success, adoption, or value).
  • Docs: docs/audit.md "What a score does not mean"; docs/testing-and-conformance.md separates protocol conformance, tested security properties, measured task effectiveness, and heuristic checks, and adds "What conformance does not show"; docs/security.md points each mitigation at the review item whose tests pin it. Positioning in README.md, docs/why-axe.md, docs/concepts.md, docs/faq.md, docs/platforms.md, and the landing page: consistent behavior for people and agents over the same application logic, reached through MCP, WebMCP, and the DOM; a published manifest does not make agents find or adopt a site. Payment and identity kinds are described as payload shapes (docs/requirements-and-kinds.md, spec/KINDS.md, docs/faq.md). README "What is and is not claimed". ROADMAP.md restructured into six ordered priorities, each labeled open SDK primitive or commercial hypothesis, followed by the deferred items.

Review 2026-09-24, item 17: evaluation harness and pilot plan

  • examples/plan-review: evaluation variants selected by PLAN_REVIEW_VARIANT at request time (lib/variant.ts): v1 the page with generic markup, v2 the page with accessible names and the Surface DOM mirror, v3 basic CRUD tools (lib/basic-tools.ts, served at POST /tools/{name}; no revision, availability, handoff, or idempotency key), v4 AXE only. Unset, the app is unchanged. PLAN_REVIEW_UI_CHANGE=1 applies the controlled UI change (Save relabeled, item column moved). A test-only snapshot endpoint beside the reset (only with PLAN_REVIEW_TEST_RESET=1).
  • examples/plan-review/eval/: a deterministic harness (pnpm eval, also pnpm example:eval): eight scenarios (simple edit, interrupted task, stale observation, two actors, unavailable control, lost response, navigation, human handoff), one scripted agent algorithm with a driver per variant (Playwright for v1 and v2, MCP for v3 and v4), outcome checks against the app's state and history, traffic and latency measurement, integration line counts, Wilson intervals, and a maintenance re-run after the UI change. Writes docs/review/2026-09-24/data/evaluation-<date>.{json,md}; the run of 2026-09-24 is committed.
  • examples/plan-review/eval/model/: an opt-in model-driven runner skeleton with the same scenarios and checks; it refuses to start without AXE_EVAL_MODEL_PROVIDER, AXE_EVAL_MODEL_CREDENTIAL_ENV, and AXE_EVAL_ACCEPT_COST=yes, and with them only prints its plan. Not run.
  • Docs: new docs/evaluation.md and docs/pilot-plan.md (a plan; no pilot run, no one contacted); docs/reference-app.md points at the harness.
  • Fixes found by the evaluation run: @axe/client honors retryable: false and no longer retries such an unavailable or rate_limited error; the reference page re-enables its buttons and keeps drafts when a request gets no answer.

The ledger as the one history (Surface contract v0.9)

  • @axe/surface: surface.record({ op, target, actor, changed?, text?, revBefore?, status?, expectedRev?, source? }) appends a change the application made outside act (a person's own control, an approval, a server push), or a refusal the surface never saw, and returns the entry. It runs no handler and does not move the revision; revBefore defaults to the revision when it is called, the text policy and the sensitive rule apply as for an act ([S-LED-8]). Entries not written by act carry source (application, or server for the bridge's); entries act writes are unchanged. New types RecordRequest and LedgerSource; LedgerEntry gains optional source and expectedRev.
  • @axe/core: an ActionProvider may declare onResult(ctx: ProviderResultContext, result); the server calls it for every result of an action that provider supplied, after the site's onResult, with the identity and siteKey the runtime established, the envelope's input and expectedRev, and handled (whether a handler produced the result). Additive; a hook that throws is logged.
  • @axe/surface/axe: both bridges implement onResult ([S-AXE-14]): a refusal the runtime made before an acting action's handler ran (a stale expectedRev, an input that fails the schema, a missing idempotencyKey), for a caller admitted under the action's auth mode, is recorded on the caller's surface with source: "server", the entry id and op, and the caller as actor, once, with no new action event. addProvider wires it. <ns>.ledger's description now says exactly what the ledger holds, and its display shows the source.
  • spec/SURFACE.md v0.9: [S-LED-1] and [S-LED-7] amended, [S-LED-8] and [S-AXE-14] added; vocabulary rows for record, source, and ProviderResultContext.
  • docs/examples/demo/plan-board.ts: "Approve March" is recorded in the ledger by the person, spanning the revision it moved; the page's ledger table marks recorded entries and server refusals. A test (docs/test/demo.test.ts, run by the docs package's test) runs the scripted demo sequence against the real script on a free port and checks the ledger has no revision gap. Found by an agent demoing the board over MCP.
  • examples/plan-review: plan.history says it lists committed changes and approval decisions and that a refused or stale write is not listed, which was already the behavior.

Relay: an agent in a signed-in person's live tab

  • @axe/relay (new package). @axe/relay/client: connectRelay(surface, { url, token | getToken, onStatus, indicator, requireApproval }) connects a page's surface to a relay over one WebSocket, answers snapshots and acts through the page's own surface.act, shows an in-page indicator with Stop and approvals (or none, for an application that renders its own), renews its token in-band, reconnects with backoff, stops on page unload, and rekey() re-identifies after a tenant switch; devToken for development. Browser-native, no Zod, no Node built-ins, about 11 kB minified. @axe/relay/server: createRelay keeps a mirror per tab that implements the surface interface, so domainActions, createAXE, and @axe/mcp serve it unchanged, over Streamable HTTP (sessions, OAuth agentAuth) and stdio; tabs listed and chosen with relay_tabs and relay_select-tab; origin patterns, tenant allowlist, development pairing on loopback (relay_pair). @axe/relay/token: mintRelayToken and verifyRelayToken, HS256 JWTs with sub, org, aud, and a lifetime of at most a day.
  • axe relay (CLI, and the package's own axe-relay bin): --dev for local development (prints the page snippet and the claude mcp add commands), --dev --stdio for Claude Code to start it, --stdio --principal --tenant for one local agent acting as a named principal.
  • spec/SURFACE.md (header version left to the release): [S-MODE-3] now names @axe/relay as the SDK's one broker; new §9.1, [S-RELAY-1] to [S-RELAY-10].
  • Docs: new docs/relay.md; a relay section in docs/security.md; docs/surface.md and docs/reference-app.md updated where they said the SDK has no broker. Vocabulary: a Relay table and axe relay.

Easy mode: derived surfaces (Surface contract v0.9)

  • @axe/surface/auto (new subpath; browser, no Zod, no Node built-ins, shares the main registry): autoSurface({ root, surface, config, observe, expose, route, hidden, revision, layout, now }) reads the rendered page's accessibility semantics and registers one entry per control, keeps it current with a coalesced MutationObserver (open shadow roots and same-origin frames included), acts through the events a person causes (pointer, mouse, focus, click(); the native value setter plus input and change; beforeinput and insertText for rich-text editors; load-more by button or scroll), waits for the page to settle, and reports changed and notices (toast and status text). The handle has refresh, coverage, configure, config, approve, elementFor, metaFor, route, expose, and stop.

  • SurfaceConfig: a plain, reviewable overlay of rules matched by key, data-surface-id, selector, or route, role, and name, setting name, object, role, id, reason, state, effect, sensitive, editable, hide, approval, group, or a real handler (the declared tier); plus routes, lexicon, policy, groups, sensitive and exclude selectors, declared entries, landmarks, and navigate. checkConfig validates it.

  • Safety defaults: a heuristic risk per derived action from role, words (destructive words anywhere; view and commit words in the verb position), styling, and surroundings, erring high; the default policy asks the person before a high-risk act, through an unavailable state with an approval_required handoff, and handle.approve(id) records the person's approval for one act. Sensitive fields (passwords, card fields, one-time codes) never report a value and are read only to agents.

  • Coverage: handle.coverage() and formatCoverage report counts by kind, tier, and name confidence, approvals, gaps (unnamed and icon-only controls, duplicates, clickable elements without a role, canvas and chart regions naming the library, cross-origin frames, virtualized grids, file inputs, closed shadow roots, unrecognized effects), stale configuration, and a rule to paste per gap.

  • autoActions in @axe/surface/axe (with autoDomains in /auto): generic tools for a derived surface (groups, navigate, set-field, run-control, load-more), the same size on every page.

  • @axe/surface/react: SurfaceProvider, useAutoSurface, useAutoSurfaceHandle; starts in an effect, re-scans on History API and router location changes, stops on unmount. Tested on React 18 (the package) and React 19 (examples/auto-react19).

  • @axe/surface: entries carry an optional source (derived, annotated, declared), reported on observe rows that are not declared; an action entry may carry a value ({ checked }, { pressed }, { selected }, { expanded }); a handler report may carry notices, returned in the act's output.

  • spec/SURFACE.md §10 ([S-AUTO-1] to [S-AUTO-13], [S-CFG-1] to [S-CFG-8]); docs/auto-surface.md; vocabulary rows under "Derived surfaces"; a headless browser check (pnpm --filter @axe/surface test:browser).

  • Naming: a surface entry's guarantee tier is tier (derived or annotated; absent means declared), distinct from a ledger entry's source (application or server). Both were added in this unreleased cycle under the same name; the entry field was renamed before release.

Integration in four steps: axe surface init, axe surface coverage, and the prompt pack

  • axe surface init [--dir] [--framework auto|react-router|next|vite-react|react|plain] [--mount <file>] [--flag <NAME>|<module>#<export>] [--flag-hook <call> --flag-import <module>] [--relay <url>|--relay-dev] [--dry-run] [--yes] [--install] [--vendor <dir>]: detects React Router 7 (app/root.tsx, honoring appDirectory), the Next App Router (app/layout.tsx), Vite React and React under any bundler (the entry that calls render()), and plain HTML (index.html), and the package manager from the nearest lockfile (npm, pnpm, Yarn classic, Yarn Berry workspaces with their root, bun). Writes a surface component (surface.tsx, or surface.js for a plain page) and an empty surface.config overlay with commented examples beside the root, and wraps the root (or a --mount layout; layout routes are listed as candidates) in one import and one element in the file's own quotes, semicolons, and indentation. Gated by default on a build-time variable (VITE_SURFACE, NEXT_PUBLIC_SURFACE; on in development, off in a production build), or on localhost for bundlers without one; expose only in development. Prints a unified diff, applies with --yes or after a prompt, and is idempotent. Never adds a dependency unless --install; prints the registry and the tarball install forms, including the overrides, pnpm.overrides, or root resolutions entry.
  • axe surface coverage <url> [--auth] [--routes] [--max-pages] [--wait] [--playwright-from] [--json] [--out]: loads Playwright lazily from the app (or prints how to install it), waits for window.__surface, calls coverage() on each listed route or up to five same-origin pages (never a sign-out link), and prints one Markdown report with each page's gaps and suggestions and the top gaps across pages. A page without coverage() but with observe() gets a basic count from the CLI; a page without a surface says why (not mounted, flag off, production build, expose off, a login redirect).
  • axe surface prompt prints packages/cli/templates/integrate-surface.md, the integration prompt a coding agent runs in any app: dry run, review, apply, install, measure, write config for the top gaps, verify by driving the app. It names the llms.txt sections it relies on; a test checks they exist.
  • The generated code imports SurfaceProvider from @axe/surface/react, SurfaceConfig and autoSurface from @axe/surface/auto, and connectRelay from @axe/relay/client, which land separately; packages/cli/src/surface/api.ts holds every guessed name and prop in one place, and the fixture typecheck stubs pin the guessed shapes.
  • Vocabulary: axe surface, axe surface init, axe surface coverage. Docs: docs/getting-started.md starts with "Add Surface to an existing app in four steps".
  • CI runs on Node 22 and 24 (was 20 and 22): jsdom, which the browser-style tests use, requires Node 22 or later. The workspace now requires Node 22 to develop. Published packages keep their declared Node range, but it is no longer tested on Node 20.
  • Security fix found by an end-to-end trial: an auto-derived surface read the relay's in-page indicator, so its Stop, Approve, and Deny were controls an agent could see, and a pending approval moved the revision so the agent's act came back stale. The scan now skips any subtree marked data-surface-ignore and the relay indicator itself; the relay marks its indicator.
  • Derived surfaces move the revision only when something an agent can act on changes (a control appears, disappears, or changes name, availability, or value), not when a table's content does, so a page that polls or updates live does not refuse every act.
  • Act notices from the top-level heuristic report only text that was not on the page before the act, so a page re-rendering its own rows is not reported as a message.
  • One approval, not two: an auto-derived surface registers its approver on the surface (a shared symbol), and the relay treats a derived approval gate as needing the person's approval and grants it when the person approves in the tab. Granting or expiring an approval does not move the revision, so the agent's retry at the same revision runs.
  • @axe/relay: @axe/mcp, @modelcontextprotocol/sdk, and ws are optional peer dependencies, needed only where a relay server runs. A browser application that imports @axe/relay/client installs none of them (verified with Yarn 4 under a seven-day registry age gate; the app's browser bundle of @axe/surface/react, /auto, and @axe/relay/client is about 99 KB minified with React external, and every entry imports cleanly in Node for server rendering).
